title.value: TSQP: Safeguarding Real-Time Inference for Quantization Neural Networks on Edge Devices
TSQP: Safeguarding Real-Time Inference for Quantization Neural Networks on Edge Devices

abstract.value: Quantization Neural Networks (QNNs) has been widely adopted in resource-constrained edge devices due to their real-time capabilities and low resource requirement. However, concerns have arisen regarding that deployed models are white-box available to model thefts. To address this issue, TEEshielded secure inference has been introduced as a secure and efficient solution. Nevertheless, existing methods neglect the compatibility with 8-bit quantized computation, which leads to severe integer overflow issue during inference. This issue could result a disastrous degradation in QNNs (to random guessing level), completely destroying model utility. Moreover, the model confidentiality and inference integrity also face a substantial threat due to the limited data representation space. To safeguard accurate and efficient inference for QNNs, TEE-Shielded QNN Partition (TSQP) are proposed, which presents three key insights: Firstly, Quantization Manager is designed to convert white-box inference to black-box by shielding critical scales in TEE. Additionally, overflow concerns are effectively addressed using reduced-range approaches. Secondly, by leveraging the Information Bottleneck theory to enhance model training, we introduce Parameter De-Similarity to defend against powerful Model Stealing attacks that existing methods are vulnerable to. Thirdly, the Integrity Monitor is suggested to detect inference integrity breaches in an oblivious manner. In contrast, existing method can be bypassed due to the lack of obliviousness. Experimental results demonstrate that proposed TSQP maintains high accuracy and achieves accurate integrity breaches detection. Our method achieves more than 8× speedup compared to full TEE inference, while reducing Model Stealing attacks accuracy from 3.99× to 1.29×. To our best knowledge, proposed method is the first TEE-shielded secure inference solution that achieves model confidentiality, inference integrity and model utility on QNNs. 2114 2025 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)

Quantization Neural Networks (QNNs) has been widely adopted in resource-constrained edge devices due to their real-time capabilities and low resource requirement. How- ever, concerns have arisen regarding that deployed models are white-box available to model thefts. To address this issue, TEE- shielded secure inference has been introduced as a secure and efficient solution. Nevertheless, existing methods neglect the compatibility with 8-bit quantized computation, which leads to severe integer overflow issue during inference. This issue could result a disastrous degradation in QNNs (to random guessing level), completely destroying model utility. Moreover, the model confidentiality and inference integrity also face a substantial threat due to the limited data representation space. To safeguard accurate and efficient inference for QNNs, TEE-Shielded QNN Partition (TSQP) are proposed, which presents three key insights: Firstly, Quantization Manager is designed to convert white-box inference to black-box by shielding critical scales in TEE. Additionally, overflow concerns are effectively addressed using reduced-range approaches. Sec- ondly, by leveraging the Information Bottleneck theory to enhance model training, we introduce Parameter De-Similarity to defend against powerful Model Stealing attacks that existing methods are vulnerable to. Thirdly, the Integrity Monitor is suggested to detect inference integrity breaches in an oblivious manner. In contrast, existing method can be bypassed due to the lack of obliviousness. Experimental results demonstrate that proposed TSQP maintains high accuracy and achieves accurate integrity breaches detection. Our method achieves more than 8× speedup compared to full TEE inference, while reducing Model Stealing attacks accuracy from 3.99× to 1.29×. To our best knowledge, proposed method is the first TEE-shielded secure inference solution that achieves model confidentiality, inference integrity and model utility on QNNs. 1. Introduction While Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have demon- strated remarkable success in various critical tasks [1], they are oftentimes excessively big and computationally expensive for resource-limited edge devices. As a prominent solution, Quantization Neural Networks (QNNs) has gained widespread attention [2], [3]. The key idea of QNN is the access to hardware inference acceleration by converting full-precision computation into efficient low-bit. Nowadays, popular deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch [4], TensorFlow [5], ONNX [6] and TensorRT [7] all support 8- bit QNNs. Furthermore, various edge computing platforms, including FPGA [8], [9], NVIDIA Jetson Series [10], and Google Coral Series [11], have implemented extensive op- timizations for 8-bit integer computations. Alarmingly, a recent large-scale study conducted on 1468 popular ML applications [12] revealed that 41% of them lack model protection mechanisms. Even 66% of pro- tected models can be easily extracted using dynamic analysis techniques. Model providers often dedicate considerable resources in training advanced models with private datasets, which are crucial in maintaining their competitiveness. Therefore, it is expected to safeguard model confidentiality by downgrading white-box models to black-box: clients can benefit from high-quality on-device inference without ability to obtain full model information through Model Stealing (MS) attacks [13], [14], [15], [16]. Recent studies have made significant advancements in preserving confidentiality of on-device models, which can be classified into two categories: cryptography-based methods and TEE-shielded methods. Cryptography-based approaches utilize techniques such as Multi-Party Computation (MPC) [17], [18] and Homomorphic Encryption (HE) [19], [20] to enable secure inference without exposing plaintext pa- rameters. While these methods offer robust security, they come with a substantial increase in computational complex- ity, leading to significant latency overheads. This poses a challenge for real-time tasks and is particularly unsuitable for resource-constrained hardware devices. On the other hand, TEE-shielded methods [21], [22], [23], [24], [25], [26] protect the privacy-sensitive components of model in TEE and offload computationally intensive operations to Rich Execution Environment (REE) for acceleration. Such methods aim to strike a tradeoff between inference speed and model confidentiality, effectively addressing the high latency drawbacks of cryptography-based methods. However, current methods would introduce severe inte- ger overflow issues in QNNs, leading to significant degra- dation in model utility. Advanced security mechanisms have been proposed to map inference computations into large finite fields (e.g. Zp with p = 2 24 − 3), and obfuscate model parameters or Intermediate Result (IR) to ensure model confidentiality. Nevertheless, this contradicts the core principle of QNNs utilizing low-bit operations for infer- 2114 DOI 10.1109/SP61157.2025.00001 MNIST_LeNet5 CIFAR10_VGG16 CIFAR10_ResNet18 CIFAR100_VGG16 CIFAR100_ResNet18 ImageNet_VGG19 ImageNet_ResNet50 Various Dataset and Model 0 20 40 60 80 100Accuracy (%) 98.06 91.02 95.23 71.79 81.12 72.08 75.79 97.95 90.83 94.72 71.31 80.55 71.43 75.04 29.8 9.93 10.68 1.57 2.74 0.13 0.19 10.23 11.73 10.21 1.07 1.44 0.14 0.11 17.67 13.67 15.72 1.25 1.39 0.33 0.13 20.26 10.02 11.25 1.75 1.86 0.22 0.42 No Shield TSQP Magnitude Shadownet T eeslice Soter Figure 1. Applying obfuscation in the low-bits- constrained space can easily lead to integer overflows, which can be disastrous for parameter-sensitive neural networks. As shown in Figure 1, the accuracy of existing SOTA meth- ods is evaluated on several QNN models. Remarkably, all of them result in significant model performance degradation (nearly random guessing). While current methods excel in expensive data types, they are not compatible with QNNs that are widely adopted at the edge. Furthermore, the model confidentiality and inference integrity are at greater risk with QNNs because of the constrained data space (refer to §4.2 and 4.4). Hence, there is an urgent need to develop secure inference approaches tailored for QNNs that can enable low- bit inference acceleration while ensuring security. To tackle the aforementioned challenges, this study in- troduces TEE-shielded QNN Partitions (TSQP), a secure and efficient inference framework tailored for QNNs. TSQP comprises three key components: Parameter De-Similarity, Quantization Manager, and Integrity Monitor. Firstly, Pa- rameter De-Similarity (refer to §4.2) is incorporated during the training phase. Leveraging Information Bottleneck the- ory [27], [28], we aim to reduce the mutual information between the private model and publicly available models, hence defend against powerful MS attacks with public priors [21]. Moreover, the quantization range is reduced [2], [29] to create space for subsequent security mechanisms, thus preventing 8-bit quantization overflow. To compensate for quantization errors resulting from range reduction, reduce- range adaptive training [30] is involved to enhance model accuracy. Secondly, during the inference phase, Quantization Manager (refer to §4.3) is devised to protect model confiden- tiality. This component shields crucial re-quantization scales within TEE, while offloading complex inference operations to REE for acceleration. Additionally, Intermediate Results (IRs) are transmitted securely using One-Time Pad (OTP) to safeguard shielded scales from key analysis attacks. Conse- quently, adversaries are unable to conduct accurate inference outside TEE or deduce plaintext model parameters from shielded scales. Thirdly, the Integrity Monitor (refer to §4.4) is tailored to detect integrity breaches such as parameter fault injections [31], [32] and result manipulation. Based on the Reproduction Theorem of Normal Distribution, the suggested integrity monitor generates oblivious Fingerprints (FPs) to conduct detection, which is indistinguishable to ad- versaries. In comparison, FPs of existing method can be dis- tinguished by adversaries, resulting in detection bypassed. Through these insights, TSQP ensures model confidentiality, inference integrity and high accuracy simultaneously, while leveraging REE for accelerated inference processing. Experiments are conducted to illustrate the efficacy of proposed method. In terms of model confidentiality (refer to §5.2), TSQP outperforms existing methodologies by offering superior defense against MS attacks. Regarding inference integrity (refer to §5.3), TSQP achieves a 100% accuracy rate with no false positives. In relation to model utility (refer to §5.4), TSQP exhibits nearly no accuracy degradation and provides over 8× faster inference acceleration compared to methods that shield full layers. To our best knowledge, the proposed TSQP is the first TEE-shielded secure inference method tailored for QNNs, which achieves model confidentiality, inference integrity and model utility simultaneously. Our main contributions can be summarized as follows: • We propose Parameter De-Similarity to defend against state-of-the-art Model Stealing attacks. In comparison to the black-box setting, TSQP merely results in a modest 1.29× increase in attack accuracy, whereas existing meth- ods achieve a approximate 4.0×. • Quantization Manager is designed to achieve model con- fidentiality while enabling access to REE for accelera- tion. TSQP effectively addresses overflow issues to main- tain high accuracy and demonstrates over 8× inference speedup compare to full TEE inference. • Integrity Monitor is tailored to provide oblivious infer- ence integrity detection, which achieves 100% accuracy with little overhead. Moreover, our detection cannot be bypassed since generated fingerprints follow the same distribution with real intermediate results. 2115
